patch.value: The vendored fork and the canonical analyzer implement the same policy, but the canonical one is more thorough at 1273 lines against 529: both parse a real syntax tree, and both reject a docstring that merely restates its identifier via a novel-word floor after camelCase tokenization and filler stripping. Verified before swapping that the canonical analyzer scans the same 32 authored non-test files, so the gate did not narrow.
Retire the vendored docstring analyzer and converge the changelog on replace mode

pm-vcs carried a 529-line local fork of the docstring analyzer plus a 774-line test for it, while the fleet enforces the canonical analyzer published as pm-ops docstrings. The release workflow also still generated the changelog in prepend mode while the gate verified replace mode.

The docstring gate is a thin launcher importing pm-ops docstrings under an exact pin, the gate still passes, coverage stays at 100 percent, and the release workflow generates the changelog in the same mode the gate verifies
